page: Microsoft Azure E96-24ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 5669 GB NVMe SSD. The instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and lacks GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Small-model LLM text generation also reaches top-tier speeds. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded decompression, and database operations fall into the average tier. Memory performance is strong, with PassMark memory scores in the top 25%, though large-block memory bandwidth remains average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E96-24ads_v7 offers high resource density by combining a massive memory footprint with a large local NVMe SSD, reducing the need for external premium storage attachments. However, the dedicated AMD EPYC processor and high memory allocation position it in a premium hardware tier. Tradeoffs include average multi-core scaling relative to its high single-core capabilities, and the absence of a GPU. This server is optimized for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and data analytics.
